catalog_quote: Stress occurs on the penultimate syllable. In words with three or four syllables minor stress occurs on the antepenultimnate syllable. The exception to this is in words of two syllables with syllabic consonants occuring as the first syllable stress occurs on the final syllable.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Kurze Vokale werden nicht bezeichnet, ´ über einem Vokal gibt den dynamischen Akzent an. Liegt dieser auf einem langen Vokal, so steht hierfür kein anderes als das Längezeichen. Sind in einem Worte mehrere Vokale als lang bezeichnet, so steht das Akzentzeichen über dem Längezeichen. Der dynamische Akzent liegt zuweilen auf dem vorangehenden Worte, Numeruszeichen oder Artikel: Z. B. ká lpek sein Kopf, mina ló lpek ihre (2) zwei Köpfe, na kró lpektuk ihre Köpfe, lá gunes die Kinder, tá mnur er weiß es. Hierbei wechselt zuweilen die Quantität des Vokals: Z. B. ó kvak Schmutz, ō reak Taro, ká nhar sein Fuß, kā sie ihr Junges. Auch ein nachstehendes Objekt kann von Einfluß auf die Betonung eines Wortes sein: Z. B. gólot es ausschütten, golót min die zwei ausschütten.
new_statements.translation: Short vowels are not marked; ´ over a vowel indicates the dynamic accent. If it lies on a long vowel, nothing but the length mark is written for it. If several vowels in a word are marked as long, the accent mark is placed over the length mark. The dynamic accent sometimes lies on the preceding word, number marker or article: e.g. ká lpek 'his head', mina ló lpek 'their (2) two heads', na kró lpektuk 'their heads', lá gunes 'the children', tá mnur 'he knows it'. In this the quantity of the vowel sometimes changes: e.g. ó kvak 'dirt', ō reak 'taro', ká nhar 'his foot', kā sie 'her young'. A following object can also influence the stress of a word: e.g. gólot 'pour it out', golót min 'pour out the two'.
new_statements.citation: Müller, Hermann (Br., M.S.C.). 1915-1916. Erster Versuch einer Grammatik der Sulka-Sprache, Neu-Pommern (Südsee). Anthropos 10/11: 75-97, 523-552. Passage on p. 76 (I. Teil, Lautlehre, §2 Vokale).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Müller gives no placement rule: stress (the 'dynamic accent') is simply marked with an acute on whichever vowel carries it in each word, i.e. treated as a lexical property; he adds that the accent sometimes falls on the preceding possessive/number marker or article rather than on the noun/verb, and that a following object can shift the accent within a verb (gólot 'pour it out' but golót min 'pour out the two'). Provisional reading 'lexical (unpredictable)' therefore means 'no rule stated, marked word by word', not a positive claim of contrastive stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated as exceptions; the shifts to a preceding article/number marker and under a following object are presented as regular tendencies ('zuweilen').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level marking (acute on the stressed vowel of each cited word), but the two observations given are phrase-level: stress can sit on a preceding possessive/number marker or article (ká lpek 'sein Kopf', lá gunes 'die Kinder', tá mnur 'er weiß es'), and a following object can move the stress of the verb (gólot vs. golót min). Based on the author's own fieldwork on Cape Orford Sulka (1899 onward), pre-phonemic notation.
new_statements.identity_note: Müller 1916 describes the Sulka of the north tip of Cape Orford, Neu-Pommern (= Wide Bay area, the main Sulka body; sulk1246 has no dialects per Tharp 1996: 77). Tharp 1996 is based on Wide Bay Sulka as well. No dialect issue.

sources.note: Lautlehre §2 (p.76): acute marks the 'dynamischer Akzent'; the accent 'liegt zuweilen auf dem vorangehenden Worte, Numeruszeichen oder Artikel' (ká lpek, mina ló lpek, lá gunes, tá mnur); vowel quantity sometimes changes with it; a following object can shift a word's stress (gólot vs. golót min). No general placement rule stated. No further stress statement in pp. 523-552 (a full-text search for stress/accent Beton/Akzent).
Datapoint list read via the values endpoint: only 9A (velar nasal) in phonology; no stress features 14A-17A for Sulka. Sources cited there are Tharp 1996, Müller 1916, Schneider 1962.
